thread.title: Q2's profit surge was the strongest in years. Here's who led the charge in Tampa Bay

author: Jeff Jeffrey
title: Q2's profit surge was the strongest in years. Here's who led the charge in Tampa Bay
text: – Tampa Bay Business Journal Sep 4, 2018, 6:22am EDT U.S. companies rebounded from a lackluster showing in the first quarter of the year with a surge in profits that's expected to fuel even more economic growth in the months ahead. The Commerce Department reported that after-tax profits among U.S. companies jumped 16.1 percent year-over-year during the quarter that ended June 30, qualifying as the largest such increase since 2012. Several Tampa Bay companies topped that national average, and four local companies more than doubled their profit in 2Q 2018 compared to the second quarter of last year. They are: PGT Innovations (NYSE: PGTI), a Sarasota window and door manufacturer, 120 percent increase in year-over-year 2Q profits; 2Q 2018 profit was $22.6 million CenterState Bank (NASDAQ: CSFL), a Winter Haven-based financial services firm, 111 percent increase; 2Q 2018 profit was $32.2 million WellCare Health Plans (NYSE: WCG), a Tampa managed care provider for government-sponsored health programs, 104.6 percent increase; 2Q profit was $151.6 million United Insurance Holdings (NASDAQ: UIHC), a St. Petersburg property and casualty insurer, 102.6 percent increase; 2Q profit was $14.7 million The boom was especially pronounced in the banking industry, which pocketed more after-tax profits than any other sector in Q2. Among U.S. financial companies, profits increased $16.8 billion in the second quarter, in contrast to a decrease of $9.3 billion in the first quarter. Meanwhile, the Commerce Department reported that profits at non-financial corporations increased $63.6 billion, compared with an increase of $32.3 billion. A Business Journals analysis of more than 3,000 publicly traded companies found that the electronics components sector saw the largest profit gains over the same period in 2017. The sector reported $15.9 billion in profit during the second quarter — $8.5 billion more than what it earned during the year-earlier period. Warren Buffett 's Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK.A) posted the largest quarterly profit of any public company in the second quarter, and it also posted the strongest year-over-year gain. The Omaha, Nebraska-based investment company netted $12 billion last quarter, marking a $7.8 billion increase over 2017's corresponding period. Berkshire’s success narrowly beat the world’s first trillion-dollar company. Apple’s (NASDAQ: AAPL) second-quarter profits topped $11.5 billion, a $2.8 billion improvement from a year earlier. Rounding out the top five were Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), which earned $8.9 billion (up $804 million); JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM), with $8.3 billion (up $1.3 billion); and Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), with $6.9 billion (up $1.7 billion). Among local companies, WellCare posted the largest profit gain in dollars. WellCare's 2Q 2018 profit of $151.6 million was an increase of $77.5 million from the year-ago quarter. Jabil (NYSE: JBL), a St. Petersburg-based electronic services firm and manufacturer, had a $67.8 million increase in profit year-over-year for its most recent quarter (the third quarter of Jabil's fiscal year), with $42.5 million in profit the three months ended May 31, compared to a loss of $25.3 million in the year-ago quarter. Tech Data (NASDAQ: TECD), a Clearwater IT distributor, had profit of $75.9 million in the quarter ended July 31, a 60 percent increase from the year-ago period. Tech Data unveiled a cost-cutting plan after its earnings release last week that is expected to result in some layoffs as the company shifts toward newer and higher margin technologies. Here's how other Tampa Bay companies stack up: Kforce (NASDAQ: TECD), a Tampa staffing firm, 2Q 2018 profit of $16.3 million, 46 percent year-over-year increase Masonite International (NYSE: DOOR), a Tampa-based door manufacturer, 2Q 2018 profit of $34.7 million, 29.2 percent year-over-year increase Roper Technologies (NYSE: ROP), a Sarasota technology and engineered products firm, 2Q 2018 profit of $228.4 million, 27.2 percent year-over-year increase Raymond James Financial (NYSE: RJF), a St. Petersburg financial services company, $232.3 million profit in the three months ended June 30 (the third quarter of the company's fiscal year), 26.6 percent year-over-year increase MarineMax (NYSE: HZO), a Clearwater recreational boat retailer, $17.4 million in profit for the three months ended June 30 (the third quarter of the company's fiscal year), 22 percent year-over-year increase AquaVenture (NYSE: WAAS), a Tampa water services firm, lost $4.9 million in 2Q 2018, an improvement from the net loss of $5.3 million in the year-ago quarter. Several Tampa Bay companies saw profits fall year-over year. They are: Helios Technologies (formerly Sun Hydraulics) (NYSE: SNHY), a Sarasota industrial manufacturer, $6.8 million in 2Q 2018 profit, down 6.7 percent year-over-year Superior Group of Companies (NASDAQ: SGC), a Seminole uniform manufacturer and branding company, $3.8 million in 2Q 2018 profit, down 12 percent year-over-year Sykes Enterprises (NASDAQ: SYKE), a Tampa call center operator, $7.2 million in 2Q 2018 profit, down 18.8 percent year-over-year Bloomin' Brands (NYSE: BLMN), a Tampa restaurant operator, $26.7 million in 2Q 2018 profit, down 23.9 percent year-over-year HCI Group (NYSE: HCI), a Tampa insurer, real estate and technology firm, $6.4 million in 2Q 2018 profit, down 32.9 percent year-over-year Health Insurance Innovations (NASDAQ: HIIQ), a Tampa technology company that distributes health insurance products, 2Q 2018 profit of $2.9 million, down 34.6 percent year-over-year Welbilt (NYSE: WBT), a New Port Richey manufacturer of commercial food service equipment, 2Q 2018 profit of $12.1 million, down 59.8 percent year-over-year Heritage Insurance Holdings (NYSE: HRTG), a Clearwater property and casualty insurer, 2Q 2018 profit of $2.4 million, down 63.7 percent year-over-year
